result.evidence_A: About 92 words, close to target. Covers the calibration problem, BW limb darkening, and phase and wavelength dependence in amount and shape. States 'twelve percent' near-IR, misreading the ~2% artifact. Omits interferometry and VLTI capability and drops the star name to 'Gem'. Coverage of the method is thin.
result.evidence_B: About 120 words, roughly 35% over target, which is a length defect. Covers Hipparcos parallax errors, the BW method, non-LTE time-dependent models, single-parametrization failure, and VLTI baselines and sensitivity for southern Cepheids. Shares the 'twelve percent' error. Future VLTI work is phrased appropriately as potential.
result.comparative_reason: Both share the near-IR percentage error. A meets the length target but omits the interferometric/VLTI element central to the paper. B overshoots length but gives materially fuller and accurate coverage of method and findings, including VLTI capability. On balance, B fulfills the rubric better.
